title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Sunsets Warning Praise And Servanthood While Standing

questions.question: What time of day is this passage about?
questions.answer: Sunset, the time of Maghrib.

questions.question: What happens to the beautiful living things from summer and fall when this time comes?
questions.answer: They pass away and disappear as winter begins.

questions.question: What sad human event does sunset make a person remember?
questions.answer: A person’s death and leaving loved ones behind.

questions.question: Where does the passage say a person goes after death?
questions.answer: To the grave.

questions.question: What big event for the world does this time also bring to mind?
questions.answer: The world will come to an end, and its people will move on to other worlds.

questions.question: What image shows that this world’s test time will end?
questions.answer: Its lamp will be put out.

questions.question: What kind of things are warned against in this passage?
questions.answer: Loving temporary things too much and treating them like they should be worshipped.

questions.question: Why is the warning strong at sunset?
questions.answer: Because sunset shows that beautiful things in this world do not last.

questions.question: What is one main idea of the passage?
questions.answer: This time reminds people that life in this world is short and they should not cling to things that fade away.

questions.question: If someone only loves things that do not last, what lesson should he learn from this passage?
questions.answer: He should remember that those things will go away and turn his heart toward what lasts.

questions.question: Which prayer time is described in the target passage?
questions.answer: Maghrib, at sunset.

questions.question: What season starts when the lovely things mentioned in the passage disappear?
questions.answer: Winter.

questions.question: How are those good-byes described?
questions.answer: They are sad and full of parting.

questions.question: What does sunset help us think about in a person’s life?
questions.answer: That one day each person will die.

questions.question: How are the people a dying person loves affected?
questions.answer: They are left in sadness.

questions.question: What happens to the people of the world when the world ends, according to the passage?
questions.answer: They move to other worlds.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen to the light of this world’s testing place?
questions.answer: It will be turned off.

questions.question: Who especially needs the warning in this passage?
questions.answer: People who give their hearts to things that are only here for a short time.

questions.question: What does the word “transient” mean here?
questions.answer: Not lasting; going away after a short time.

questions.question: What feeling does the passage give about sunset: only joy, only silliness, or a serious reminder?
questions.answer: A serious reminder.

questions.question: What natural change at day’s end begins this passage?
questions.answer: The sun is setting.

questions.question: What does this time remind people about summer and fall?
questions.answer: Their beauty fades and comes to an end.

questions.question: What lesson about this world can children learn from that picture?
questions.answer: Pretty things in this world do not stay forever.

questions.question: What personal change does the passage connect with this time of day?
questions.answer: A person leaving this life through death.

questions.question: What is left behind when a person dies?
questions.answer: The people he loves.

questions.question: What place is mentioned after death?
questions.answer: The grave.

questions.question: Besides one person’s death, what much bigger ending is mentioned?
questions.answer: The death of the whole world.

questions.question: What happens to the world’s people at that time?
questions.answer: They go on to other worlds.

questions.question: What warning does this give about loving worldly things too much?
questions.answer: We should not treat short-lived things like they are our real forever beloveds.

questions.question: What is the best short summary of the passage?
questions.answer: Sunset teaches that life and worldly beauty pass away, so people should not attach themselves to what cannot last.

questions.question: What prayer time is linked with the ideas in this passage?
questions.answer: The sunset prayer, Maghrib.

questions.question: What happens to the gentle and beautiful beings from warm seasons when winter begins?
questions.answer: They vanish and are gone.

questions.question: Are these changes shown as happy parties or sad partings?
questions.answer: Sad partings.

questions.question: What does this teach about changes in nature?
questions.answer: Nature changes, and its beauty does not remain the same forever.

questions.question: What does the passage say a human being will do at death?
questions.answer: Leave loved ones and enter the grave.

questions.question: Why might this make a reader feel serious?
questions.answer: Because it reminds us that life in this world ends.

questions.question: What future event for the whole world is described?
questions.answer: The world will die and its inhabitants will leave it.

questions.question: What object in the passage stands for this world as a place of testing?
questions.answer: A lamp.

questions.question: What happens to that lamp?
questions.answer: It is extinguished.

questions.question: According to the passage, what kind of love is a mistake?
questions.answer: Loving passing things as if they were the true ones to hold onto.

questions.question: At what part of the day does the target passage begin?
questions.answer: At sunset.

questions.question: What happens to the lovely things from summer and autumn at that time?
questions.answer: They disappear as the cold season starts.

questions.question: What mood does the passage give with this picture?
questions.answer: A sad and thoughtful mood.

questions.question: What does sunset remind us about every person’s life?
questions.answer: Every person will die one day.

questions.question: When that happens, what separation takes place?
questions.answer: The person parts from loved ones.

questions.question: What new place is entered after that separation?
questions.answer: The grave.

questions.question: What does the passage say will happen when the world itself dies?
questions.answer: Its people will leave for other worlds.

questions.question: What does the ending of the world’s lamp show?
questions.answer: This world’s time of testing will not go on forever.

questions.question: What kind of beloved things are called unsafe to depend on?
questions.answer: Things that fade, change, and do not last.

questions.question: What wise choice does the passage push a reader toward?
questions.answer: Not giving the heart fully to temporary things.

questions.question: Which moment is being described: sunrise, noon, or sunset?
questions.answer: Sunset.

questions.question: What happens to the nice creations of summer and fall when winter starts?
questions.answer: They pass away from sight.

questions.question: What word best fits the good-byes in the passage: cheerful or sorrowful?
questions.answer: Sorrowful.

questions.question: What event in a person’s life does this scene help us remember?
questions.answer: Death.

questions.question: After death, what place does the passage mention first?
questions.answer: The grave.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the end of the whole world?
questions.answer: The world will die, and its people will move on.

questions.question: Where do they move to?
questions.answer: To other worlds.

questions.question: What happens to the light of this testing place?
questions.answer: It goes out.

questions.question: What kind of people receive a strong warning here?
questions.answer: Those who attach themselves to things that do not last.

questions.question: What is the passage teaching about things in this world?
questions.answer: They are temporary, so we should not treat them like they will stay forever.
